title: Pin-ended beam-column with equal end moments: midheight deflection

source.work: McGuire, W., Gallagher, R. H., Ziemian, R. D., Matrix Structural Analysis
source.location: Example 8.3, Equation f (the member of Example 9.3)
source.notes: input data and targets read on the cited pages; nothing of the source is reproduced

analysis: Plane (x-y) problem of the source modelled in 3D with the global Y axis vertical, so that the source's x, y and theta_z are the model's X, Y and rz. In-plane bending is about local z for every member (default orientation), hence the source's I is the section's Iz. The source gives in closed form (small-displacement theory) the midheight deflection of a pin-ended bar under an axial load P and end moments M0 = alpha P L (single curvature): delta = alpha L [sec(sqrt(P/EI) L/2) - 1]. Numeric instance: the member of Example 9.3 (L = 8 m, A = 1.27e4 mm^2, I = 3.66e7 mm^4, E = 200,000 MPa) with alpha = 1.25e-4 as in the statement of Example 9.3 and P = 600 kN chosen here (the source shows the response of this member only as a curve). Column along +Y, base a pinned, top b held laterally; moments -M0 (about Z) at a and +M0 at b bend the member toward +X. Second-order analysis, one member, no shear deformation. Plane stability problem: the source's model has no out-of-plane degrees of freedom. Here the out-of-plane DOFs (uz, rx, ry) of every node are held and Iy = 1000 Iz, so that no out-of-plane buckling mode precedes the in-plane modes compared; J is a placeholder.

targets.precisionNote: evaluated here in double precision from the expression printed in the source (Example 8.3, Eq. f); tolerance = policy floor 1e-6
targets.sign: deflection toward +X = +local y of the vertical member (default orientation)
